businessId.meta.title: What is a Business ID?
businessId.meta.description: A Business ID is the verified profile behind a Startup Value Index score: identity, evidence and capabilities in one record. Five levels, consent-based sharing.
businessId.eyebrow: The verified profile behind your score
businessId.headline: One Business. One Trusted Identity.
businessId.subhead: A Business ID is the verified profile behind your Startup Value Index score — your evidence, verification level and capabilities in one record — so investors, accelerators and grant panels can trust what you claim, without re-verifying it every time.
businessId.what.title: What a Business ID is
businessId.what.intro: Four ingredients bundled into one reusable record — verified once, presented on your terms, revocable at any time.
businessId.what.identity.title: Verified identity
businessId.what.identity.body: ASIC/ABR/ABN checked, directors matched, domain and email owner confirmed. The identity anchor for everything else on your profile.
businessId.what.evidence.title: Evidence
businessId.what.evidence.body: Traction, financials, contracts, IP — stored encrypted, hash-anchored in an audit log, cited inline in your Trust Report.
businessId.what.capabilities.title: Capabilities
businessId.what.capabilities.body: What your business can actually do — sector, offering, team skills, tooling — scored on the 13-area rubric.
businessId.what.reusable.title: Reusable
businessId.what.reusable.body: One record, many share packages. Send a signed link to an investor today, a buyer tomorrow, a grant panel next week — always current, never re-typed.
businessId.levels.title: Five verification levels
businessId.levels.intro: Each level adds a checkable claim on top of the previous one. Public /id/{slug} profiles surface the badge for the level you have reached.
businessId.level1.title: L1 — Self-declared
businessId.level1.body: You have created a Business ID with a name, jurisdiction hint and email. Not sufficient for a public profile.
businessId.level2.title: L2 — Identity verified
businessId.level2.body: ASIC/ABR/ABN record matched, domain ownership confirmed, email owner verified. Minimum bar for a public /id/{slug} profile.
businessId.level3.title: L3 — Financials attested
businessId.level3.body: Financial statements attested by a qualified accountant (CA/CPA/IPA in AU, equivalent overseas). Practical bar for investor and procurement diligence.
businessId.level4.title: L4 — Independently audited
businessId.level4.body: Financial statements audited by an independent registered auditor. Required for Series A+ diligence and material procurement contracts.
businessId.level5.title: L5 — Cross-jurisdictional
businessId.level5.body: Evidence and verification present in a second jurisdiction (used by the AU-VN corridor cohort). Includes DKKD/MST alongside ASIC/ABR.
businessId.pillars.title: 13-area analysis — 4 pillars
businessId.pillars.intro: The same 13-area rubric applies to every Business ID. Investors compare apples with apples; founders know exactly which areas need evidence.
businessId.pillar1.title: Leadership & People
businessId.pillar1.a2: Culture, org design and hiring pipeline
businessId.pillar2.title: Strategy & Commercial
businessId.pillar3.title: Ops & Performance
businessId.pillar4.title: Tech & Digital
businessId.sharing.title: How sharing works
businessId.sharing.consent.title: Consent-based
businessId.sharing.consent.body: Nothing on your Business ID leaves your control unless you create a share package. Each package selects specific evidence and audiences.
businessId.sharing.expiry.title: Time-limited
businessId.sharing.expiry.body: Every share link carries an expiry (default 30 days). Recipients see a countdown. After expiry, the link 404s — no accidental long tails.
businessId.sharing.revocation.title: Revocable, audited
businessId.sharing.revocation.body: Revoke instantly at any time. Every view is logged with timestamp, IP, and (if the viewer is signed in) their Business ID — hash-chained for tamper evidence.
businessId.badge.title: Badge widget
businessId.badge.intro: Embed your verified badge on your website, LinkedIn or email signature. Renders your current verification level, last update date, and a link to your public /id/{slug} profile — updates in real time when your level changes.
businessId.badge.caption: Sample badge: Verified Business ID · Level 3 · updated Jul 2026. Copy the embed snippet from your dashboard.
businessId.cta.title: Create Your Business ID
businessId.disclaimer: Nothing on this page is financial or legal advice. Verification confirms what the record says, not the underlying business decision. Auschain PTY LTD · ACN 659 615 111 · ABN 79 659 615 111 · Sydney NSW.

meta.solutions.investor.title: Startup due diligence for investors, in minutes
meta.solutions.investor.description: Screen an Australian startup in minutes on one 8-dimension SVI rubric, reviewed by a C-suite of AI agents, valued in AUD. Pay per report or trial Scout.
solutions.investor.headline: Screen a deal in minutes on one rubric — then send every founder you pass on the reasons why.
solutions.investor.persona: Add a startup you are evaluating. BlockID scores it on the same 8 SVI dimensions it applies to every company, runs the whole C-suite of AI agents over its evidence, audits the claims, and re-scores it as the company changes — so a first pass compares like with like, and the second pass is already waiting.
solutions.investor.benefits.title: Why an investor uses BlockID instead of a deck and a prompt
solutions.investor.benefit1.title: One rubric for every deal
solutions.investor.benefit1.body: 8 SVI dimensions × 12 growth phases, scored the same way for every startup in your pipeline. Scores are comparable across companies, each judgement carries its reasoning, and you can disagree with one line rather than with the whole number.
solutions.investor.benefit2.title: A whole C-suite reviews each startup
solutions.investor.benefit2.body: A C-suite of AI agents — CFO valuation, CLO legal with ESIC and s708, CMO market, CRO funding readiness, CTO, CHRO and more — each with its own domain module and Australian context. Then an auditor checks the claims and flags what the evidence does not support.
solutions.investor.benefit3.title: The startup's own evidence, accumulating
solutions.investor.benefit3.body: Evidence vault, weekly SVI snapshots, score history and data room: the company updates itself and you see the delta, without waiting for a founder email. Your data belongs to your startup. We store it so every report builds on your own evidence and the AI reasons on your case. Founder-consented access tiers control who sees what.
solutions.investor.faq.title: Frequently asked
solutions.investor.faq.a1: A full Trusted Business Report on a startup you enter: the 8-dimension SVI score with its reasoning, an AUD valuation range with the methods shown, the C-suite review, the auditor's flags and a next-step plan, as a PDF. No subscription needed, and an ATO tax invoice on the charge.
solutions.investor.faq.a2: Scout ({scoutPrice} a month) includes {scoutReports} reports a month, {scoutStartups} tracked startups, a weekly Progress Radar with score deltas, stage changes and new evidence, deal-flow browse and a watchlist. Firm ({firmPrice}) and Program ({programPrice}) add seats, white-label reports and cohort tools. Every plan starts with a 7-day free trial, card required — nothing is billed if you cancel before day 7.
solutions.investor.faq.q3: Is a score a substitute for diligence?
solutions.investor.faq.a3: No. It is a triage layer built from what the founder gave us and what is publicly available, audited for unsupported claims. Nothing on the platform is financial or investment advice, and every decision remains yours.
solutions.investor.faq.a4: Fund ({fundPrice} a month) takes Program to {fundSeats} seats, {fundStartups} tracked startups and unlimited Trusted Business Reports, with your own rubric weights on every batch, the weekly Progress Radar across the whole portfolio, the quarterly LP / sponsor export and read-only API access. Same 7-day free trial, card required. Funds that need SSO or unlimited seats talk to us about VC Enterprise.
solutions.investor.disclaimer: Not financial, investment or legal advice. Scores and valuation ranges are generated from founder-supplied and publicly available information; investment decisions remain your own. Auschain PTY LTD · ACN 659 615 111 · ABN 79 659 615 111 · Sydney NSW.
meta.solutions.accelerator.title: Score your whole cohort on one startup rubric
meta.solutions.accelerator.description: Score every startup in a cohort on one 8-dimension SVI rubric, reviewed by a C-suite of AI agents, then show sponsors the progress. 14-day trial.
solutions.accelerator.eyebrow: For accelerators, incubators and university programs
solutions.accelerator.headline: Score the whole cohort on one rubric, then show sponsors the progress — automatically.
solutions.accelerator.persona: Every startup in your program is scored on the same 8 SVI dimensions across 12 growth phases, reviewed by a C-suite of AI agents with an auditor behind them, and re-scored as it changes — so the cohort compares like with like and sponsors see movement, not memory.
solutions.accelerator.benefits.title: What a program gets
solutions.accelerator.benefit1.title: One rubric across the whole cohort
solutions.accelerator.benefit1.body: 8 SVI dimensions × 12 growth phases, applied the same way to every company you take in, so two startups side by side is a real comparison. Batch scoring queues a whole application round or cohort on one rubric — with your own weights across the 8 dimensions if you want them — scores it off-peak overnight, and lands in a cohort table you can sort and download as CSV.
solutions.accelerator.benefit2.title: A C-suite review for every founder
solutions.accelerator.benefit2.body: A C-suite of AI agents reviews each startup — valuation, legal and ESIC, market, funding readiness, tech, team — with an auditor flagging unsupported claims. Your mentors start from a diligence-grade read instead of a deck.
solutions.accelerator.benefit3.title: Progress you can show, company by company
solutions.accelerator.benefit3.body: Each startup's evidence accumulates and its score is re-taken weekly, so movement between sessions is visible and a sponsor update is assembled from the record rather than from memory. Your data belongs to your startup. We store it so every report builds on your own evidence and the AI reasons on your case. Founder-consented access tiers control who sees what.
solutions.accelerator.journey.title: What a cohort's first 90 days look like
solutions.accelerator.journey.step1.head: Set the cohort up
solutions.accelerator.journey.step1.b1: Add every startup in the cohort and run its first score on the shared rubric.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step1.b2: Assign mentors — roster, check-ins and notes sit beside the score.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step1.b3: Read the gaps the first scores name across the whole cohort.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step2.head: Work the gaps
solutions.accelerator.journey.step2.b1: Run sessions against the dimensions the cohort scores worst on.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step2.b2: Fill each company's data room in the order investors ask for it.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step2.b3: Re-run the scores and compare them against the first pass.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step3.head: Demo day
solutions.accelerator.journey.step3.b1: Each founder shares a live investor link instead of a PDF.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step3.b2: Publish the founders who consent to a public profile at /listings/{slug}.
solutions.accelerator.journey.step3.b3: Export the sponsor / LP report for the cohort from the cohort table.
solutions.accelerator.faq.title: Frequently asked
solutions.accelerator.faq.q1: Can we score a whole cohort in one run?
solutions.accelerator.faq.a1: Yes. Tick the startups in your evaluations workspace, choose Batch score, name the round and optionally set rubric weights for the 8 dimensions. Every company gets a full Trusted Business Report on the same rubric, scored off-peak overnight from your plan's included reports, and you get a sortable cohort table — SVI, weighted score, stage, movement since last score, top strength and top gap per startup — plus a CSV export.
solutions.accelerator.faq.q2: Can our sponsors or LPs see the underlying startups?
solutions.accelerator.faq.a2: Only what you or the founder chooses to share — founder-consented access tiers control who sees what. Every Programs plan, from the Intake link up, includes a packaged sponsor / LP report per cohort: cover, cohort summary (size, median SVI, movers), a one-line read on each startup, and the methodology and disclaimers, exported from the cohort table and ready to print or save as PDF.
solutions.accelerator.faq.q3: How does pricing work for a program?
solutions.accelerator.faq.a3: Programs are billed annually. The Intake link is {intakePrice} a month ({intakeAnnualPrice} a year) — {intakeReports} reports a month, {intakeStartups} tracked startups, {intakeSeats} seats — and Cohort 25 is {cohortAnnualPrice} a year for a cohort of {cohortStartups} startups with {cohortReports} reports a month and {cohortSeats} seats; both start with a 14-day free trial, card required. Any startup you enter can also be reported on pay-as-you-go for {reportPrice}. Multi-cohort accelerators take Cohort 100; programs that need SSO, unlimited seats or white-label reports talk to us through Contact Sales.

compare.faq.a2: For anything that has to stand on its own in a transaction, a dispute, a tax matter or a court: a share buy-back, a family-law settlement, an employee share scheme valuation for the ATO, an expert report. compare.sources.1: developmentcorporate.com (2026) — general models give systematically different verdicts on identical decks (GPT-4o vs Claude) and hallucinate founder histories, competitors and market figures; 85% of VCs use AI daily, 12% with a governed workflow.
compare.sources.2: MicroVentures — AI can hallucinate or invent facts, carries confirmation bias, and gives limited information on how it reached a conclusion; use it only with human intervention.
compare.sources.3: VC Lab (July 2026) — general models can confidently produce wrong information; do not upload confidential documents without checking the data policy.
compare.sources.4: VCBench, arXiv 2509.14448 — language models beat human precision only when given a consistent, anonymised rubric.
compare.sources.5: Multi-agent VC due-diligence framework, arXiv 2605.13110 — single-prompt language models lack role separation and evidence tracing.

meta.methodology.title: Methodology — how the Startup Value Index is scored
meta.methodology.description: The 8 SVI dimensions and their owner agents, the evidence ladder, ABN verification levels, the hash-chained audit log and how every score is versioned.
methodology.title: How the Startup Value Index is scored — and what stops it being gamed
methodology.subtitle: Eight dimensions, one evidence ladder, a verification level per business and an audit trail nobody can quietly edit. This page states the rules the engine actually runs; the calibration page shows how well they hold up.
methodology.dims.title: What the index measures
methodology.dims.intro: Every SVI score is a composite of these eight dimensions. Each has one accountable C-level agent and a fixed set of evaluation criteria. The names here are read from the same table the engine, the report chapters and the evaluator dossier use — they cannot drift apart.
methodology.dims.weightsNote: Dimension weights are shown to authenticated evaluators inside a report, not published here — a public weight table is a recipe for writing to the rubric rather than building the company.
methodology.ladder.title: How much a claim is worth depends on who can check it
methodology.ladder.intro: Every signal the engine reads carries a confidence level. The level scales how far the dimension score moves the index: a self-declared claim moves it a fifth as far as a third-party-verified one.
methodology.ladder.level.self_declared: The founder said so — text in a description, a form or a deck.
methodology.ladder.level.public_url: A public page we can open backs the claim (website, LinkedIn, app-store listing).
methodology.ladder.level.document_upload: A document is on file — deck, contract, cap table, bank statement — but nobody outside the company has checked it.
methodology.ladder.level.connected_sourc: Read by machine from the source of record over OAuth: GitHub, Google Analytics, Xero, Stripe customers.
methodology.ladder.level.transaction_dat: Money that moved — Stripe or Xero revenue and payouts, pulled from the ledger, not typed in.
methodology.ladder.level.third_party_ver: A named BlockID reviewer checked the evidence against an external record (ABR, ASIC, a signed contract) and signed the row.
methodology.caps.title: Who may set which level
methodology.caps.intro: The level is capped by the origin of the evidence, never by what the evidence says. Writing "audited" or "ASIC-registered" in a description does not raise anything.
methodology.caps.founder_text.rule: Prose never grades itself: a description is self-declared, or public-URL when it links to a page we can open. Writing "ASIC audit" changes nothing.
methodology.caps.founder_upload.rule: An upload counts as a document. It cannot post itself as connected, transactional or third-party verified.
methodology.caps.connector.rule: Machine-read from the source of record via OAuth; revenue and payouts are transaction data, everything else is a connected source.
methodology.caps.reviewer.rule: Only a named human reviewer can mark a row third-party verified, after the founder requests review. The approval is audit-logged.
methodology.verification.title: Six rungs from "no ABN" to continuous monitoring
methodology.verification.intro: Separately from the evidence on each claim, the business itself sits on a verification ladder. The rung is recomputed from the inputs every time — an ABN that goes Cancelled or an attestation that lapses drops the level, it is never grandfathered.
methodology.verification.col.label: Name
methodology.verification.multiplierNote: The multiplier scales the evidence confidence between {min} and {max}. It is bounded: a business at L5 whose evidence is all self-declared is still scored as self-declared — verification says the company is real, not that its claims are proven.
methodology.audit.title: Every change is hash-chained
methodology.audit.p1: Every mutating API call — an upload, a score, a reviewer decision, a share — writes one row to an append-only audit log. Postgres computes each row's hash from its content and the previous row's hash, so editing or deleting a row breaks every hash after it.
methodology.audit.p2: A nightly job re-computes the whole chain and cross-checks the last verified checkpoint. The result is published on the public status page as audit_chain: ok, broken or unknown.
methodology.audit.p3: Reviewer approvals, connector syncs and rescoring all live in this log, which is what lets a report state who verified what and when.
methodology.provenance.title: Which model wrote which chapter is on the record
methodology.provenance.p1: The deterministic score never touches a language model. Narrative chapters do, and every run records the model that produced each chapter and an auditor stamp: whether the text is grounded in the evidence rows, how many statements went uncited, and whether the auditor revised it.
methodology.provenance.p2: We do not make claims about any vendor's model being better than another's. Models are routed by availability and cost and can change between runs; the record of which one ran does not.
methodology.versioning.title: Three version numbers travel with every report
methodology.versioning.note: A stored report keeps the versions it was produced with, so an old report is never silently re-scored by a newer rule set.
methodology.data.title: Data ownership
methodology.sources.title: Open Australian data behind the score
methodology.sources.intro: Three open Commonwealth registers are bulk-ingested under their published licences and matched to a startup only by its verified ABN: the Australian Business Register (entity status, age, GST), GrantConnect grant awards and the ATO R&D Tax Incentive transparency report. Rows from these registers land at the connected_source rung of the evidence ladder, never higher. Commercial reports are cited with a link only, never copied.
methodology.sources.attributionNote: Attribution statements are printed exactly as each licence requires. Register data describes the legal entity, not the founder; the R&D register figure is shown as a band with the register’s own value, never re-estimated.
methodology.sources.cohortNote: Cohort percentiles use at least 20 peers. When fewer than 20 scored startups exist at a stage, the register cohort (ABR entity age, GST, grants, R&D registration) is used and labelled as such; below 20 there too, a static benchmark is shown and labelled an estimate.
methodology.calibration.title: How well the score predicts outcomes
methodology.calibration.body: The score is only worth publishing if it is checked against what actually happened. The calibration page reports the backtest: index at first score versus raise, revenue and survival outcomes on the AU cohort.
methodology.cta.title: See the rules applied to a real startup
execution.title: Execution
execution.intro: Structured facts about what you and your team have already done. These drive the Founder & Team score directly (a fixed rubric, not keyword matching) and appear as the Founder Execution card in your report.
execution.score.title: Execution score
execution.score.rubric: Rubric: exits 30 · prior raises 15 · years in domain 20 · role coverage 15 · full-time 10 · worked together 5 · GitHub 5.
execution.score.capped: Self-reported — shown at the 70 cap until an evaluator checks your references or your LinkedIn PDF confirms years and employers.
execution.exits.title: Prior exits
execution.exits.hint: Companies you founded or led that were acquired, listed, or wound down. A shutdown still counts — investors read it as learning.
execution.raises.title: Prior raises
execution.raises.hint: Rounds you closed before — this company or a previous one.
execution.roles.title: Who holds which seat
execution.roles.hint: Name the person in each role, or leave blank. Two distinct names count as a co-founder team.
execution.full_time.label: Full-time %
execution.full_time.hint: Share of the founding team on this full-time (0–100).
execution.worked_together.label: Worked together before
execution.github.label: GitHub URL
execution.github.hint: Your user or organisation page. Connect GitHub under Evidence to score commit activity instead of the URL alone.
execution.import.hint: LinkedIn → Profile → More → Save to PDF. We read years, employers and exits from it, mark them as parser-confirmed, and never keep the file.
execution.import.unavailable: The LinkedIn parser is not available in this build — fill the fields by hand.
execution.import.applied: Imported from LinkedIn: {fields}. Review, then save.
execution.import.exits: The export mentions {n} exit(s) — add the company names under Prior exits.
digest.why_moved.sentence: Why it moved: evidence confidence is now capped by its source (self-declared ≤ document, connector, reviewer) and your ABN verification level (L{level}) now weights the score.
